A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ColPali method and ViDoRe benchmark. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval evaluations, latency measurements, ablations, and qualitative analyses in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 2 and 4 and ablation results in Figure 4 and Table 5.

M1.justification: Both versions use PaliGemma, 128-dimensional embeddings, late interaction, hardest-negative contrastive training, and five query-augmentation tokens. The mathematical corrections clarify the existing procedure; they do not establish a changed algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: The same five academic tasks and five practical topics in English and French remain in Table 1. Training coverage and the TabFQuAD adaptation experiment are unchanged; Appendix E corrects existing examples without adding coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 4, and 5 retain the same comparators: BM25 and BGE-M3 under the same ingestion variants, Jina-CLIP, Nomic-vision, SigLIP, and the same trained model variants. No comparator is added or removed from a corresponding experiment.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes two descriptions of Idefics2's post-resampling patch count from 60 to 64. This is a limited correction to the reported configuration, matching the already-present Figure 4 label and footnote 12, without evidence of rerunning experiments. Splits, metrics, training budgets, and latency protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6 retains the same model-size, patch-count, vision-tuning, query-token, loss, and French-adaptation analyses with unchanged evidence in Figure 4 and Table 5. Appendix C's similarity-map analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. Table 3 retains the sparse-BM25 embedding-size mean and standard deviation of 1.56 ± 0.51 KB, and Appendix B.5 retains the same latency averaging procedures.

E6.justification: The numerical results and rankings in Tables 2–5 and Figures 3–4 are unchanged. For example, ColPali's average NDCG@5 remains 81.3 and average Recall@1 remains 72.7. Reported latency measurements and qualitative heatmap findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Section 2 changes the score range from nonnegative to unrestricted real values. Section 4.1 corrects the positive score from LI(d_k, q_k) to LI(q_k, d_k), relevant because late interaction is asymmetric, and replaces the undefined negative-document symbol p_l with d_l. Appendix B.2 still retains the older loss definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: ViDoRe for visually rich document retrieval and ColPali for effective image-based retrieval with faster indexing and low querying latency. No central claim is added, strengthened, or narrowed.

C2.justification: The interpretations of multilingual performance, late interaction, model-size tradeoffs, and similarity maps remain unchanged. The limitations concerning document types, high-resource languages, synthetic-query bias, abstention, and infrastructure support are also retained.

D1.justification: The two 60-to-64 patch-count corrections improve technical documentation in Section 6, although another sentence still says 60. The implementation information in Appendices A–B, training hyperparameters, hardware, generation prompts, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The PaliGemma reference is updated from a model-release entry to the formal Beyer et al. paper describing the same underlying work. This bibliographic update does not change the substantive related-work coverage, novelty claims, or research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds Bilel Omrani to the author list and an explicit equal-contribution footnote, updates the PaliGemma bibliography entry, and makes isolated wording and punctuation edits. The section structure and almost all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix E swaps two Energy query captions so that the photovoltaic-savings and California-demand questions match their existing document images. Other changes mainly concern page and column reflow; the numbered figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves accuracy by correcting score definitions in Sections 2 and 4.1 and misleading query-image pairings in Appendix E, while retaining the empirical evidence. The cleanup is incomplete: Appendix B.2 preserves the old loss definitions, and Section 6 still contains one 60-patch reference. These are useful but limited gains.
